subject.title: fix(logging): scale heap-pressure thresholds with V8 limits

question: Should gateway heap-pressure diagnostics use the proposed 50% warning and 75% critical fractions of V8’s effective heap limit, capped at 4 GiB and 6 GiB, as the default restart-protection policy?
rationale: The implementation is a narrow fix for a demonstrated false critical event, but the selected fractions and caps intentionally define when existing large-heap gateways will emit warnings or trigger stability handling.

options.title: Accept adaptive defaults
options.body: Adopt the V8-relative thresholds and caps so configured heap capacity, rather than a fixed 2 GiB value, governs default heap-pressure diagnostics.

options.title: Adjust the operating policy
options.body: Keep the V8-derived design but choose different ratios or caps after comparing the desired warning and restart behavior for large and constrained deployments.

options.title: Preserve fixed defaults
options.body: Retain the current fixed thresholds and address large-heap deployments through an explicitly documented operator-controlled setting instead.

recommendation.title: Accept adaptive defaults
recommendation.body: Adopt the V8-relative thresholds and caps so configured heap capacity, rather than a fixed 2 GiB value, governs default heap-pressure diagnostics.
